summary: XML injection in the encoder of Saxy. Saxy.Encoder does not neutralize the -- sequence in XML...
description:
XML injection in the encoder of Saxy. Saxy.Encoder does not neutralize the -- sequence in XML comment content: escape_comment/2 returns the comment binary unchanged in every clause and only appends a space when the comment ends in a single -, so neither an interior -- nor a full --> is escaped or rejected before the encoder wraps the content in the <!-- and --> delimiters.

When an application serializes attacker-controlled text as a comment, through Saxy.XML.comment/1 or a raw {:comment, text} simple form child, the attacker can close the comment early with --> and inject arbitrary sibling markup into the serialized document. A downstream parser then sees elements, attributes, and text that the application never built. Where the document is rendered as HTML or SVG, the injected markup executes as stored cross-site scripting; where it is consumed by another XML processor, the attacker can forge data that the producing application never emitted. Documents that Saxy only parses are not a vector.

This issue affects saxy: from 0.7.0 before 1.7.0.

summary: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in ninenines cowlib allows an...
description:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in ninenines cowlib allows an unauthenticated remote peer to exhaust the memory of an HTTP/2 endpoint via HPACK-indexed header fields.

cow_http2_machine:headers_decode/4 in src/cow_http2_machine.erl decodes every HEADERS block with cow_hpack:decode/3. It bounds the compressed block size and the number of fields, but not the size of the decoded header list that RFC 9113 section 6.5.2 places under SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE. A peer stores one header value of up to the dynamic table size (4096 bytes by default) and then references it with one-byte indexed fields, so about 100 bytes on the wire decode to a header list of about 390 KB. A consumer that copies the decoded values, as Cowboy does when cowboy_http2:headers_to_map/2 joins repeated cookie fields into one binary, allocates that amount for every stream. The total across streams and connections is not bounded.

This issue affects cowlib: from 2.7.0 onward.

summary: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in ninenines cowboy allows an...
description:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in ninenines cowboy allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust connection process memory over HTTP/1.1.

Once a request has been received in full and its handler is still running, cowboy_http:parse/2 in src/cowboy_http.erl appends every further byte that arrives on the keep-alive connection to the connection buffer and returns to the receive loop without parsing it. The socket stays in active mode and no limit applies to this buffer: max_request_line_length, max_headers and the other parser limits only take effect once the handler returns and parsing resumes, and the only timer in this state is idle_timeout (default 60 seconds), which is reset on every received chunk. A client can therefore send an arbitrary amount of data on one connection for as long as the handler runs, and a few connections to an endpoint that holds requests open can drive the Erlang VM into out-of-memory conditions.

This issue affects cowboy: from 2.18.0 onward.

cwes.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

summary: The AutomatorWP  WordPress plugin before 6.0.7 does not check that the user completing its Zoom...
description: The AutomatorWP  WordPress plugin before 6.0.7 does not check that the user completing its Zoom and AWeber integration connections is allowed to do so, allowing unauthenticated attackers to replace the stored integration credentials with their own and divert the data the site sends to those services into an account they control. Exploitation requires the integration to already be connected and knowledge of the site's OAuth client identifier.

summary: The Ever Accounting  WordPress plugin before 2.3.3 does not restrict the file path supplied to...
description: The Ever Accounting  WordPress plugin before 2.3.3 does not restrict the file path supplied to its CSV import routine to an allowed directory, allowing users with its custom Accounting Manager role (which does not have administrator privileges) to delete arbitrary files on the server, such as wp-config.php, which takes the entire site offline.

summary: The Static Snapshot WordPress plugin through 0.2.1 does not sanitise shell metacharacters in a...
description: The Static Snapshot WordPress plugin through 0.2.1 does not sanitise shell metacharacters in a user-supplied value before concatenating it into operating-system commands run by the server, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands on the host.

cwes.name: Improper Control of Generation of Code

summary: The All-in-One Video Gallery  WordPress plugin before 5.1.0 does not escape a video's stored...
description: The All-in-One Video Gallery  WordPress plugin before 5.1.0 does not escape a video's stored thumbnail URL before outputting it in the admin video list, and does not sanitise that value when it is written outside its own editor, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against administrators.

summary: The PublishPress Revisions: Duplicate Posts, Submit, Approve and Schedule Content Changes...
description: The PublishPress Revisions: Duplicate Posts, Submit, Approve and Schedule Content Changes WordPress plugin before 4.3.1 does not correctly restrict who may publish content, allowing users such as Contributors who can edit but not publish to make unreviewed posts and pages publicly live, bypassing the intended editorial approval workflow.

summary: The MC4WP: Mailchimp for WordPress plugin before 4.15.0 does not validate that the Mailchimp...
description: The MC4WP: Mailchimp for WordPress plugin before 4.15.0 does not validate that the Mailchimp audience a sign-up form or bundled integration subscribes a visitor to matches the audience configured by the site owner, allowing unauthenticated visitors to subscribe arbitrary email addresses to any other audience in the site's connected Mailchimp account.

summary: The PublishPress Revisions: Duplicate Posts, Submit, Approve and Schedule Content Changes...
description: The PublishPress Revisions: Duplicate Posts, Submit, Approve and Schedule Content Changes WordPress plugin before 4.3.1 does not verify that a user is permitted to read a given post before returning its content through its revision-comparison feature, allowing any authenticated user, including a Subscriber, to read the title, content and excerpt of any other user's private, draft, pending, scheduled or trashed post.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

summary: The Anti-Spam, Spam FireWall by CleanTalk WordPress plugin before 6.91 does not escape a...
description: The Anti-Spam, Spam FireWall by CleanTalk WordPress plugin before 6.91 does not escape a commenter-supplied value before outputting it on an administrative spam-review screen, allowing unauthenticated users to inject arbitrary web scripts that execute in the browser of an administrator who reviews flagged comments.

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

summary: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine ('Server-Side Template...
description: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine ('Server-Side Template Injection') in Apache OFBiz 24.09 before 24.09.08 on all platforms allows a remote authenticated attacker holding only a stock non-administrative account to execute arbitrary operating system commands as the OFBiz process user, by using the updateLayoutImage event, which writes DataResource fields with no permission check, to retype an attacker-created DataResource as an FTL template evaluating its own primary key, then using the resulting FreeMarker evaluation to plant an OFBiz Form Widget whose use-when attribute runs unsandboxed Groovy. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 24.09.08, which fixes this issue.

summary: Use of Web Browser Cache Containing Sensitive Information vulnerability in Drupal Media Alias...
description: Use of Web Browser Cache Containing Sensitive Information vulnerability in Drupal Media Alias Display allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels. This issue affects Media Alias Display versions: from 0.0.0 to 2.1.3, from 3.0.0 to 3.0.3.

summary: Use-after-free in the DOM: Core & HTML component. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 159,...
description: Use-after-free in the DOM: Core & HTML component. This vulnerability was fixed in Firefox 159, Firefox ESR 115.44, and Firefox ESR 153.6.

summary: A flaw was found in the Micrometer user-event metrics listener of Keycloak, a solution for...
description: A flaw was found in the Micrometer user-event metrics listener of Keycloak, a solution for integrated identity and access management. The issue occurs when the listener is configured to include the idp tag. An unauthenticated attacker can send requests to the identity broker login endpoint using arbitrary provider aliases, causing the system to create an unlimited number of metric time series. This can lead to excessive memory consumption and degrade the performance of both the server and its monitoring tools.

cwes.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

summary: A flaw was found in the Admin REST API of Keycloak, an identity and access management solution....
description: A flaw was found in the Admin REST API of Keycloak, an identity and access management solution. The endpoints used to retrieve groups associated with a specific role do not properly check for individual group visibility permissions. This allows a delegated administrator with basic search privileges to view detailed information about all groups assigned to a role, bypassing intended security restrictions that should limit their view to specific groups.

summary: A flaw was found in the Conditional OTP authenticator of Keycloak, an identity and access...
description: A flaw was found in the Conditional OTP authenticator of Keycloak, an identity and access management solution. The issue occurs when the system evaluates specific HTTP headers to determine if a one-time password (OTP) should be skipped, but fails to verify if those headers came from a trusted source. This could allow an attacker who already has a user's password to bypass the second-factor authentication by providing a specially crafted header in their request.

summary: A flaw was found in the User-Managed Access (UMA) implementation of Keycloak. The issue occurs in...
description: A flaw was found in the User-Managed Access (UMA) implementation of Keycloak. The issue occurs in the authorization token endpoint when processing permission tickets. If two different users own resources with the same name, the system incorrectly merges the permissions from both resources when one user requests an authorization token. This allows an attacker to gain access scopes on a victim's resource that were never intended to be shared.
